title: Underwater Cultural Heritage (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2018
short_title: Underwater Cultural Heritage (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would repeal the Historic Shipwrecks Act 1976 and provide transitional arrangements supporting its replacement by the companion Underwater Cultural Heritage Bill 2018.
It would carry existing protections, permits, notices and the shipwreck register into the new framework, while updating related heritage and maritime legislation to match.
Its substantive schedules would begin with section 3 of the companion legislation and would not start at all if that provision did not commence.
changes: References in the Australian Heritage Council legislation would shift from historic shipwrecks to underwater cultural heritage.
Pending permit applications under the old law would be deemed refused, allowing applicants to apply under the new framework.
Existing exploration or recovery permits would be treated as permits granted under the replacement law.
Evidentiary certificates issued under the old legislation would remain valid after its repeal.
summary.affected: Existing permit holders, pending permit applicants and people possessing or controlling protected shipwreck articles would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Melissa Price
speeches.brief: The Underwater Cultural Heritage Bill 2018 updates the Historic Shipwrecks Act 1976, extending protection to human remains, sunken aircraft, and sites outside jurisdictional waters, while strengthening enforcement powers and public awareness. It covers approximately 7,500 historic shipwrecks and other underwater cultural heritage sites in Australian and Commonwealth waters.
